The rule never looks at the size or the number of entries of an archive: it fires on whole-archive calls and on tar calls with no filter, and a filter that only checks paths silences it. Neither its firing nor its silence says anything about a size or entry-count limit.

The sole explicit pattern selects filter="fully_trusted", disabling tar path and link filtering, not maximum expanded-size or file-count budgets. Those budgets require separate controls; the pattern neither examines them nor proves they are absent.

The rule matches an entry name used as a path with no prefix, local-path, dot-dot or relative-path test in the loop; it has no notion of sizes or entry counts, so a loop with a path check and an unbounded copy stays silent.

The rule fires on every whole-archive extraction call and on entry names joined to a folder, and recognizes no guard of any kind, so it neither sees a size or entry-count limit nor falls silent when one is present.
The rule examines only whether entry names stay under the target folder; it never looks at the type of an entry, so it says nothing about links.
The rule examines entry names against the target folder and, for whole-archive calls, a length comparison; it never looks at the type of an entry, so it says nothing about links.

The Go patterns reach the transport-security age, the sniffing protection and the framing option of the security middleware, and the development flag changes only its transport-security options; none reads or removes a content security policy, so a Go project can lose its policy header while the rule stays silent.

The Rust rule looks at the Rocket Shield fairing, and no policy of that fairing is a content security policy: creating it empty or disabling a policy never removes one, so the rule says nothing about this requirement.

The Go patterns reach only the legacy framing option of the security middleware, which the requirement says cannot be relied on; nothing reads the policy's frame-ancestors directive or a policy being removed, so the rule can fire on a state that is no failure and stay silent on the failure.

The Rust rule looks at the Rocket Shield fairing, whose framing policy is the legacy header the requirement says cannot be relied on, and no policy of the fairing carries frame-ancestors, so the rule says nothing about the directive the requirement asks for.
